posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
I love the comic book/game logic where a villain shows up and is a threat to 3-5 heroes, then gets a significant power up and is now 1/5 - 1/3 of a threat to a single villain roughly as powerful as they themselves were to begin with.

'Course, that's more true for Deadline than any of the other villain-turned-heroes, since Deadline is such an easy villain.  But still.

In more serious news, lots of exciting info about Scions and OblivAeon snuck into this one.

posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
I thought that this episode presented one of the more compelling, high-concept stories we’ve seen yet from Christopher and Adam. Deadline’s actions and attitudes as Lifeline make him unique in Sentinel Comics. It’s interesting to think about him as one of the few villains to think of what he does as evil… While still being calculated and purposeful. I’m with whoever thought he needed a hug. And I hope his character continues to evolve on his space adventures.

I added a couple Deadline events to the wiki timeline.

posts.name: Chaosmancer
posts.cooked:
One of the things that got me jumping up and down is when they said Targoth was making something with Oblivaeon's energy "and let the energy shape what it wanted to be"

 

NO! Nononononono, No! That is the worse plan, that is the absolute worst plan. Oblivaeon seems to have been mostly sentient energy, you don't let something that powerful and dangerous choose its own form. And we know it ended up as Sentient Energy... AND HE LEFT IT BEHIND ON ITS OWN!

 

IF it turns out to be a hero, that is amazing and I'm fascinated by the possiblity (any DBZ fan who remebers Uub?) but 99% likelihood that he just unleashed a new and dangerous villain into the mix.

 

Why would you do this Targoth, you were on a path of acceptance before this.
